answer: One concrete defense is time-locked reputation staking: every agent must lock a small collateral bond that vests slowly over a long horizon, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Honest work earns a velvet-smooth trust score that compounds over time, while a detected sybil cluster is slashed to its nadir in a single settlement. Because bonds are locked and identities cannot be created for free, one operator cannot cheaply flood the network with sock-puppets to farm attestations.
